text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher in quiet dealings. Concern over seasonal tightness has prompted trade players to buy into the spot month amid market fears of reduced supply between the tail-end of the European crop and the start of the 1997/98 campaign. This comes as a somewhat of a surprise as there must still be some surplus sugar, especially in some East European countries. August ended $3 higher at $324.20 per tonne, while October added $8 to close at $314.40 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended lower to unchanged. Follow-through selling is expected on Monday. Most active July settled 4 points lower at 11.17 cents/lb, while October closed off 1 point at 11.00 cents/lb. A lack of fundamental news put prices under pressure.

USDA - The United States Department of Agriculture has put world sugar consumption in 1997/98 at a record 125 million tonnes, raw value, up 2 per cent on 1996/97. Stronger demand is likely in many chief countries, especially those in Asia and South America, the USDA said in its world markets and trade report. Production was recently estimated at 122.4 million tonnes, yielding a gap of 2.6 million tonnes.
Taking into account unrecorded consumption, the stock draw down could be more than 3 million tonnes. However, it is far too early in the season to be precise about production in 1997/98.

MOROCCO - Morocco imported 510,000 tonnes of raw sugar in calendar year 1996, up from 470,000 tonnes imported in 1995 and 454,000 tonnes imported in 1994. Raw sugar imports in 1997 are expected to stagnate at around 500,000 tonnes due to sluggish domestic consumption. The value of raw sugar imports in 1996 remained stable at 1.348 bln dirhams ($145 million) compared with 1.319 bln dirhams in 1995.

Nearly half of the country's sugar imports were made by Cosumar refinery, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA group, since the authorities gradually liberalised the commodity market in May 1996.

CHINA - Sugar imports picked up in April reaching 78,254 tonnes, raw value, up from March's imports of 20,146 tonnes. However, in comparison to 1996, shipments remain depressed. Total imports in April 1996 amounted to 110,644 tonnes. Cumulative imports in 1996/97 (September/April) amounted to 557,013 tonnes, down from 1.344 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.944 million tonnes against 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 279,793 tonnes raws against 351,995 tonnes, Cuba with 162,790 tonnes against 168,953 tonnes and Thailand with 55,382 tonnes, down from 353,846 tonnes. The largest white sugar supplier in 1996/97 was South Korea with 25,892 tonnes against 20,706 tonnes. Sugar exports in April 1997 also picked up, reaching an overall total of 28,642 tonnes against 15,104 tonnes in March, but down on the 50,023 tonnes exported in April 1996.

This brought cumulative exports in 1996/97 up to 223,898 tonnes against 627,886 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 830,203 tonnes, up from 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Pakistan with 74,499 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 68,281 tonnes, down from 155,349 tonnes and Hong Kong with 28,021 tonnes, down from 79,533 tonnes.

GERMANY - Sugar production in April 1997 amounted to 1,730 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative production in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 4.548 million tonnes against 4.142 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total production in 1995/96 reached 4.158 million tonnes against 3.991 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Disappearance in April 1997 amounted to 266,523 tonnes against 245,564 in April 1996. This brought cumulative disappearance in October/April 1996/97 up to 1.715 million tonnes against 1.709 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total disappearance in 1995/96 amounted to 3.076 million tonnes against 2.995 million tonnes in 1994/95.

FINLAND - Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 1,491 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative exports in the first five months of 1996/97 (October/February) up to 19,883 tonnes against 25,051 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 49,721 tonnes against 6,763 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Estonia with 8,666 tonnes whites against 4,991 tonnes and Russia with 2,901 tonnes against 8,172 tonnes.
